provenance.note: Home-based program: street address, phone and provider name are not shown.

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional: A child with food allergies lacked a food allergy plan.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Food Allergy Emergency Plan Signed by Parents and Health Care Professional (26 TAC §747.3619)

occurrences.finding: Primary Caregiver Annual Training - Required Special Topics without specific hours: The primary caregiver was missing training in immunization and three hours in  management techniques, leadership, or staff supervision.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Primary Caregiver Annual Training - Required Special Topics without specific hours (26 TAC §747.1309(d))

occurrences.finding: Children's Products- Annual Certification: Form 2885, pertaining to Children's Product Certification, has not been revised since 02/03/2023.
Written Operational Policies - Parent Rights: The operational policies lacked details regarding "parents' rights".
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Operational Policies - Parent Rights (26 TAC §747.501(9))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check determination - If ineligible then you must immediately remove subject from operation and confirm to CBCU receipt of notice letter: The primary caregiver allowed a household member to be present  at the operation after the CBCU has notified the operation that the person is ineligible to be present.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check determination - If ineligible then you must immediately remove subject from operation and confirm to CBCU receipt of notice letter (26 TAC §745.635(2))

occurrences.finding: Required Immunizations Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current: One child did not have updated immunization available during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Immunizations Records, Exceptions, and Exemptions Current (26 TAC §747.613(b))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Health Statement: 3 out of 4 child files reviewed did not contain current health statements from the child's physician after being enrolled for 12 months.
Weapons In Homes Kept in Locked Cabinet, Inaccessible to Children: A household member has two unloaded firearms in the closet. The firearms are not in a locked cabinet.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Weapons In Homes Kept in Locked Cabinet, Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §747.3505(a))

occurrences.finding: Emergency Preparedness Plan - Communication Procedures: The emergency preparedness plan was missing the following items:   How children will be evacuated or relocated to the designated safe area or alternate shelter, including specific procedures for evacuating or relocating children who are under 24 months of age, who have limited mobility, or who otherwise may need assistance in an emergency, such as children who have mental, visual, or hearing impairments;    Communication, including:  (A)The emergency telephone number that is on file with us; and  (B)How you will communicate with local authorities (such as fire, law enforcement, emergency medical services, health department), parents, and us;  How you will continue to care for the children until each child has been released
occurrences.violation_type_title: Emergency Preparedness Plan - Communication Procedures (26 TAC §747.5003(2))

occurrences.finding: Primary Caregiver Annual Training - Required Special Topics without specific hours: The caregiver was missing training for the previous training year in the following topics: 1)  Preventing and responding to emergencies due to food or an allergic reaction 2) Understanding building and physical premises safety 3) Handling, storing, and disposing of hazardous materials, 4) Prevention, Recognition and reporting of abuse/neglect.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Primary Caregiver Annual Training - Required Special Topics without specific hours (26 TAC §747.1309(d))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used for Under Two: Two children under the age of two years were observed watching television in the main classroom during the inspection. Note: this was corrected during the inspection when the caregiver turned the TV off.
